name: FreeBSD
summary: A Unix-like operating system whose kernel combines process, filesystem, and networking subsystems with modular storage and jail-based operating-system virtualization.

features.name: Integrated kernel subsystem model
features.description: FreeBSD provides process, filesystem, networking, and device functionality through cooperating kernel subsystems exposed through system calls and kernel interfaces.
benefits: Provides a coherent Unix operating-system boundary
Allows subsystems to share kernel services and resource mechanisms
costs: Kernel-wide faults can affect unrelated workloads
Subsystem coupling and synchronization increase implementation complexity

features.name: Jail operating-system virtualization
features.description: FreeBSD jails virtualize selected filesystem, user, process, and networking views for contained processes, with VNET providing a distinct network stack when configured.
benefits: Provides operating-system-level isolation without a guest kernel
Supports distinct network and resource configurations
costs: Jails do not provide hardware-virtual-machine isolation
Security and isolation depend on kernel policy and jail configuration

features.name: Modular storage transformation stack
features.description: FreeBSD GEOM composes storage transformations such as partitioning, mirroring, and encryption as a modular provider/consumer stack beneath filesystems and applications.
benefits: Composes storage policies without embedding them in each filesystem
Supports layered administration and replacement of storage providers
costs: Layered failures and metadata interactions complicate diagnosis
Performance and semantics depend on the selected stack

mathematical_views.question: How do processes, files, sockets, devices, and kernel subsystems connect across system-call operations?
assumptions: The graph abstracts locking and interrupt details
Subsystem interfaces define typed ownership and lifecycle edges

mathematical_views.question: Which host resources and views are shared, virtualized, or restricted for a jail?
assumptions: A jail is modeled as a constrained kernel view rather than a second kernel
Network isolation depends on configured VNET and related options

mathematical_views.question: How do GEOM providers transform and expose storage to consumers?
assumptions: Providers and consumers form an ordered data path
The model does not claim every composition is valid or failure-transparent
